thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT -> PROD: broad TLS handshake failures observed against edge LBs :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Severity: P1. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Regions: eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-northeast-1. On-call: @alice.sre

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED 2250000000
incident-bot: Channel: #incidents
incident-bot: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/tls-handshake-checklist

alice.sre: Ack, I'm taking command. Seeing sharp spike in Envoy TLS rejects + upstream 5xx. Paging net and platform: @bob.net @sam.platform

bob.net: joining. SYN/TCP ok, TLS aborts. Quick openssl test fails on multiple edge nodes:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect edge-eu-01.redwood.net:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_3
CONNECTED(00000003)
139784:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:tls_alert.c:1102
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

harry.support: multiple enterprise customers hitting errors ~12:04 UTC. Support queue rising. Adding affected accounts to incident doc.

carlos.eng: PKI telemetry: cert rotation kicked off at 12:02:30 UTC for edge-pop (wave-5). I also see a permissions repair job ran at 11:59:50 UTC against cert-distribution bucket. Will pull logs.

dana.prod: posting preliminary status update to status page. Notifying account teams for impacted customers.
erin-ops: statuspage: https://status.redwood.com/incident/2250000000 (temp)

alice.sre: Working timeline (WIP):
- 11:59:50 UTC: automated PKI perms repair (job PKI-REPAIR-77) ran and logged IAM object changes
- 12:02:30 UTC: cert rotation for edge-pop started (wave-5)
- 12:03:45 UTC: first synthetic checks failing in eu-west
- 12:04:10 UTC: pager fired

bob.net: grabbing Envoy and socket logs. Envoy excerpt from edge-eu-01 shows both unreadable key and handshake alerts:
```
[envoy][12:03:58] TLS handshake failed: private key load error: permission denied: open /etc/edge/certs/api.redwood.com.key
[envoy][12:03:58] TLS alert: handshake_failure from 10.11.12.13
```

bob.net: tcpdump on an affected border router shows ClientHello split across segments; second segment missing on some paths. pcap snippet:
```
12:03:57.801 IP client -> edge 443: seq 1:128 len 127  # ClientHello part 1
12:03:57.802 IP client -> edge 443: seq 128:256 len 128 # ClientHello part 2
```
Some routers only see the first segment. Looks like MTU/fragmentation issue on the peering path. I also see a peering MTU change at 11:55 UTC to 1420 (CHG-10456) in net change logs.

carlos.eng: checking cert-distribution: there are S3 403 errors at 12:02:58 when edge tried to fetch private key blobs. The perms repair job appears to have removed read perms on the `private_keys/edge/` prefix for ~40s. Uploading log: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2250000000/pki-403s.log

alice.sre: So two independent issues overlapping: (1) PKI perms change caused temporary inability for some edges to read private keys during rotation, (2) peering MTU change caused ClientHello fragmentation and loss. Either alone can cause handshake failure; together they widened blast radius.

alice.sre: Immediate mitigations to run now:
- Pause and rollback cert rotation wave-5 for nodes that failed key load.
- Apply TCP MSS clamp on eu-west and eu-central edge hosts to prevent fragmentation.
- Revert PKI perms repair and re-run with canary checks.

sam.platform: I'll pause rotation and run preflight checks. Running rollback for wave-5 now:
```
infra-cli certs rollback --service edge-pop --wave 5 --to previous
```

netops-bot: Rollback job initiated 12:05:10 UTC across wave-5 nodes.

bob.net: Applying MSS clamp & enabling PMTU probing to affected edge hosts now. Command:
```
for h in $(edge-instances --region eu-west-1 --tag edge); do ssh $h sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1; ssh $h sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu; done
```

netops-bot: MSS clamp applied to 12/12 eu-west-1 edge hosts at 12:07:30 UTC.

bob.net: After MSS clamp, reran openssl s_client: handshake completes on test clients. Envoy shows successful accepts; synthetic checks recovered for many eu-west tests at 12:09 UTC.

dana.prod: customer error rates falling but a few accounts in APAC still exhibit errors; likely wave scheduling differences. Support reaching out.

carlos.eng: PKI perms repair reverted at 12:06:45 UTC and re-applied correctly with canary at 12:08:00 UTC. Verified S3 reads for private_keys complete at 12:08:15 UTC. Uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2250000000/cert-distribution.log

erin-ops: monitoring shows decrease in errors; keeping 60m watch. Any remaining actions?

alice.sre: Quick hypothesis status inline:
- H1 PKI perms/ACL change -> confirmed (S3 403s correlated with Envoy key-load errors). Owner: @carlos.eng (confirmed)
- H2 Peering MTU/fragmentation -> confirmed (tcpdump fragments + peering CHG-10456). Owner: @bob.net (confirmed)
- H3 VPC peering route drift -> no evidence at this time. Owner: @alice.sre (no)

sam.platform: For immediate follow-ups I'll add a canary pre-check to rotations: ensure canary node can fetch and successfully load key into Envoy before proceeding with wave. (infra#PR-6001)

bob.net: Net follow-ups: require explicit MSS tuning or automatic clamp when peering MTU != 1500; add PMTU blackhole detection synthetic. (NET-1122)

carlos.eng: PKI follow-ups: add ACL-change canary and auto-rollback on S3 403 spike; add ACL dry-run mode. (PKI-881)

dana.prod: I'll prepare customer-facing post-incident message including timeline, affected window (12:02-12:10 UTC peak), and mitigations. Owner: @dana.prod

erin-ops: assigning postmortem to @alice.sre. Please include timeline, customer impact summary, artifacts, and the action items above. Also capture handoff notes: I'm handing the watch to @sam.platform at 20:00 UTC.

alice.sre: acknowledged. Drafting postmortem at docs/postmortems/incident-2250000000-draft.md. Artifacts to attach: 
- pcap: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2250000000/clienthello_fragments.pcap
- envoy logs: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2250000000/envoy-edge-logs.tar.gz
- cert distro logs: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2250000000/cert-distribution.log
- timeline: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2250000000/timeline.md

harry.support: Support will send targeted comms to impacted accounts and attach incident link. Flagging top-10 impacted customers for priority outreach.

netops-bot: Monitoring stable for 18 minutes. Auto-close scheduled in 42 minutes if no regressions.

alice.sre: Thank you everyone. Leaving channel open on 60m watch. If anything reappears, re-page immediately. :thumbsup:
